definitions.definition: A made-up word for the idea that you know your own perspective, so you exist in truth.
definitions.example: Like saying 'I see things my way, so I'm real.'

definitions.definition: Latin for 'therefore I am' — a famous phrase from philosopher Descartes.
definitions.example: Like 'I think, therefore I exist.'

definitions.definition: Your personal way of seeing or understanding things.
definitions.example: Like wearing glasses that make everything look blue — your lens is how you view the world.

definitions.definition: The system of methods used to do research or solve a problem.
definitions.example: Like a recipe for baking a cake — the steps you follow to get a result.

definitions.definition: Turned into a clear, official set of rules or steps.
definitions.example: Like writing down the rules of a game so everyone knows how to play.

definitions.definition: Expressed clearly in words.
definitions.example: Like explaining your idea so your friend gets it perfectly.

definitions.definition: A check to see how well a document (like the U.S. Constitution) is being followed.
definitions.example: Like a teacher checking if students are following the class rules.

definitions.definition: A small test to show that an idea can work in real life.
definitions.example: Like building a tiny model of a bridge to see if it holds weight before building the real one.

definitions.definition: When different things come to the same conclusion or result.
definitions.example: Like two friends who each guess the same number without talking.

definitions.definition: Designed or built on purpose to achieve a specific result.
definitions.example: Like building a machine that always makes the same toy — it's engineered to do that.

definitions.definition: The ability of an AI to think and figure things out on its own, without help.
definitions.example: Like a student solving a math problem without looking at anyone else's paper.

definitions.definition: Not recognizing the true worth or importance of something.
definitions.example: Like thinking a $100 bill is only worth $10.

definitions.definition: Systems or setups where AIs argue with each other to reach agreement.
definitions.example: Like a debate club where people argue to find the best answer.

definitions.definition: Unfair preferences or slants that affect judgment.
definitions.example: Like always picking your favorite team to win, even if they're not the best.

definitions.definition: Agreement that happens naturally, without being forced or arranged.
definitions.example: Like two friends both deciding to wear blue shirts without planning it.

definitions.definition: Agreement that is created on purpose by design or pressure.
definitions.example: Like a teacher making all students agree on an answer by giving hints.

definitions.definition: A rule that says if you believe one method is better, you must use it consistently.
definitions.example: Like if you think studying alone is best, you shouldn't then study in groups.

definitions.definition: Plural of corpus — large collections of text used to train AI.
definitions.example: Like a library of millions of books that an AI reads to learn.

definitions.definition: A short summary at the start of a research paper.
definitions.example: Like the blurb on the back of a book that tells you what it's about.

definitions.definition: Different in kind or type, not just in amount.
definitions.example: Like the difference between an apple and a car — not just more or less, but completely different.

definitions.definition: Involving multiple AI systems working together.
definitions.example: Like a team of robots each doing a different job to build a house.

definitions.definition: Repeating a process to make something better each time.
definitions.example: Like editing an essay over and over to fix mistakes.

definitions.definition: A test to see if different AIs agree on how well the Constitution is being followed.
definitions.example: Like asking several judges separately if a law is fair, then comparing answers.

definitions.definition: Total or average scores from combining multiple results.
definitions.example: Like adding up all your test scores and dividing by the number of tests.

definitions.definition: A way of judging based on what the original writer meant, not what people think now.
definitions.example: Like reading a letter and asking 'What did the writer want to say?'

definitions.definition: A result that is very different from all the others.
definitions.example: Like one student scoring 100% when everyone else scored 50%.

definitions.definition: Conditions that would prove a theory wrong.
definitions.example: Like saying 'If I see a black swan, then my theory that all swans are white is false.'

definitions.definition: Short for Biaxiosum AI Evaluation System — a method for testing AI agreement.
definitions.example: Like a recipe for checking if AIs think the same way.

definitions.definition: All the studies and papers on a particular topic.
definitions.example: Like all the books and articles about dinosaurs.

definitions.example: Like a checklist a teacher uses to grade essays the same way every time.

definitions.example: Like a student seeing someone else's answers and changing their own.

definitions.definition: A simple system to show if something is good (green), uncertain (yellow), or bad (red).

definitions.definition: An AI that looks at all results, checks for agreement, and makes a final decision.
definitions.example: Like a referee who watches the game and makes the final call.

definitions.definition: Kept secret or closed until a certain time.
definitions.example: Like a sealed envelope that can't be opened until the right moment.

definitions.definition: The process of checking how much different results agree.
definitions.example: Like comparing answers from several students to see if they match.

definitions.definition: A set of steps for handling results that are very different from others.
definitions.example: Like a special procedure for a student who gets a very different score.

definitions.definition: AI systems that give results different from the majority.
definitions.example: Like a student who answers differently from everyone else.

definitions.example: Like two students giving the same wrong answer because they used the same bad textbook.
